body:
CANONICAL: installing an Engram build and cutting stores over (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03; rev 4 on 2026-10-27 replaces the projection-repair procedure with the checked-in text at e0e038d2, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md Authority and Git). The controlling text is AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, Authority and Git, and docs/features/full-store-migration.md. Greg, 2026-09-22: "ideally we don't want to have interruptions".

1. JUDGE THE CHANGESET FIRST, because `readiness` checks only schema and policy admission, not what rows contain.
- Durable rows change (a mapped column, a record reshaped under its id, data named as retired, a durable derived row computed differently, a retired schema object, or a projection the new build no longer declares). Then import must teach the conversion by name with counts, and EVERY live store needs migration export and import (one-way, ids unchanged, the old file kept as the backup), WHATEVER readiness reports. This case still means stopping to ask Greg. `different_build_schema` is one signal of it, not its definition.
- Only the derivation of a table or search index that projection repair rebuilds changes. Then treat every live store as `projection_repair_required`. Under the standing approval the MERGER, not the coordinator, commits, pushes and carries out the cutover (AGENTS.md since e0e038d2; Greg 2026-10-27, Advisor #2134: „Przeciez mozecie zainstalowac engrama sami. Kontrolujecie wszystkie sesje”).
- Procedure for that case:
  - Only if the new build was VERIFIED to refuse an unconverted store without writing to it (check readiness on a copy: projection_repair_required, mutation_enabled=false) does the Merger install it IMMEDIATELY before the agreed plain TermAl restart, keeping the old exe as a backup. Otherwise both coordinators agree a cutover plan before it lands.
  - Greg's only act is that plain restart (stop, then `cargo run --release`). He runs no script.
  - After the restart, once no engram.exe started before the install is alive (compare start times to the install time), the Merger runs the documented step on every live store: the full `doctor --repair-projections`, or the narrower one-time step the changeset documents. Then readiness reports all ready.
  - If the restart is put off, the Merger reinstalls the old build until the next agreed moment. Done 2026-10-27: installed 16:56:38Z, rolled back 17:13:06Z after Greg deferred the restart. Every new process meanwhile was refused.
  - Until the cutover completes, nothing else builds from that master into the installed path, and the landing report says the installed build stays.
- Code facts behind this (verified 2026-10-27 at e3ca0fcb): work_service/service.rs caches the MCP writer only after a SUCCESSFUL open, so a refused open retries on the next call; the note index is maintained in app code, not by triggers. So no old-build process may be alive when stores are converted, and new-build processes refused before conversion recover by themselves.
- Reference script: target\landing\note-index-convert-after-restart.ps1.
- Migration steps: export with the old build and import with the new; tell the active sessions first, choose an idle window, stop every consumer, convert, and swap the files, keeping the old store file as the backup.
2. READINESS ON EVERY LIVE STORE with the new build. Count ~/.engram/projects before each landing rather than trusting a list. As of 2026-10-27 there are 6: Engram, TermAl, CV, fit_friends, questly, PhoenixCodeNav.
3. THE ORDINARY CASE (ready, no durable change): build the release from the committed tree. Install with a NO-GAP SWAP:
   1. copy the new exe to C:\Users\grzeg\.cargo\bin\engram.exe.new and verify its sha;
   2. rename the installed engram.exe aside into C:\Users\grzeg\.engram\backups\engram-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<old build12>.exe;
   3. IMMEDIATELY rename .new to engram.exe.
   Never leave a gap (Fable2 #943, 10-09). Use the explicit .exe path; Git Bash `cp` to a suffix-less name once wrote an unstartable file. Verify the sha and the readiness build_fingerprint and revision (no +dirty). Stop nothing: running MCP servers and sidecars keep the old build until they exit.
4. A migration tool run must never see engram.exe change mid-apply (two builds writing one store).
